cards.title: How it works today
cards.text: What's built for progression in v0.1, in five parts. Mark any part that's off.
cards.why: The questions after this one build on it, so it's worth a quick look first.

parts.title: Levels
parts.text: Permanent. Each level gives +12% HP and +9% damage. Every hero alive in the room gets XP for each kill, and a level-up mid-fight heals 25%.

parts.title: Coins
parts.text: Enemies drop them. A wipe keeps half, retreating keeps all, a win keeps all. There's nothing to spend them on yet.

parts.title: Loot
parts.text: Chests give trinkets into a satchel. You only keep the satchel by beating the boss; a wipe or a retreat loses it. A win adds one bonus trinket.

parts.title: Trinkets
parts.text: One slot per hero, equipped at camp. Eight so far: Last Breath, Volatile Charm, Frost / Ember Ring, Venom Fang, Vampire Tooth, Iron Skin, Swift Boots.

parts.title: Depth
parts.text: Pick a depth at camp. Winning unlocks the next one. Each depth makes enemies about 22% stronger, and camp shows a recommended level.

cards.title: What coins buy
cards.text: Coins pile up with nothing to spend them on. What should camp sell?
cards.why: Without a use, coins and the 'keep half on a wipe' rule mean nothing. This is the main reason to go back into a dungeon you've already beaten.
cards.pick: A camp shop: a few trinkets that change each visit, and unlocking new heroes (farmer, barbarian) for a big price.
cards.details:
Other things coins could buy, later: a second trinket slot, rerolling the shop, healing potions taken into a run, or a talent reset.

I'd keep it to trinkets and heroes first, so coins have one clear meaning: more options for your party.

cards.title: Talent points
cards.text: Stats grow by themselves; talents are chosen at camp. What shape should the choices take?
cards.why: This is what you'll tinker with between runs, so it sets how much planning the game asks of you.

options.label: A small tree per hero
options.text: A point per level, three short branches (archer: frost, fire, dodge).

options.label: Unlock specials at set levels
options.text: Planned extras (group hit, pierce) at levels 3, 6, 9.

options.label: Tree plus specials
options.text: Option a, with the specials as each branch's last node.

cards.title: Leaving at a floor's end
cards.text: Should you be able to leave after a floor and keep the loot found so far, or only by beating the boss?
cards.why: Right now every run is all-or-nothing. A choice at each floor's end gives you a push-your-luck moment, which is a real decision in a game you mostly watch.
cards.pick: Yes: at each floor's end, leave with that floor's loot, or push on. Pushing on and winning adds a bonus trinket.
cards.details:
This softens the rule you set ("you must beat the dungeon to take loot out"), so it's your call. A middle option: leaving early keeps only one item of your choice from the satchel.

The Retreat button would stay as it is: keep coins, lose the satchel.

cards.title: Choosing a dungeon
cards.text: Camp has a depth number to pick. Should it offer a few different dungeons instead?
cards.why: You said choosing the dungeon should be the main decision. A number alone is only 'harder or easier'; dungeons with a twist make the choice about your party too.
cards.pick: Yes: three dungeon cards each visit. Each has a depth, a twist (Flooded, Rat nest, Oil works) and a reward to match.
cards.details:
Example: "Oil works, depth 4: lots of oil and fire, rewards an Ember Ring." A party with the frost archer might avoid it; one with an Ember Ring might seek it out.

The twists would reuse things that already exist (hazards, enemy mixes) at first.

cards.title: A second trinket slot
cards.text: Each hero holds one trinket. Should a second slot open up?
cards.why: Two trinkets on one hero is where combos start (Frost Ring plus Volatile Charm, say), and you love things that combine.
cards.pick: Yes, earned: each hero's second slot opens at level 5.

cards.title: Party size
cards.text: Once farmer and barbarian join, do all heroes go in, or do you pick a party?
cards.why: Picking a party makes heroes you leave at home matter less, but turns each dungeon into a team-building choice.
cards.pick: Pick 3 from everyone you've unlocked. Heroes at home still get a little XP, so nobody falls far behind.

cards.title: Last Breath timing
cards.text: Last Breath says once per floor, but it actually comes back every room. Which should it be?
cards.why: Every room makes it very strong: a hero wearing it can't die in one hit, ever.
cards.pick: Once per floor, as its description says.
